decided_by: project founder ("Do all 4", 2026-11-21), on the reviewed audit
inclusion_rule: A row is a passage in a primary text, at an inspected edition, that shows divine beings gathered with a ruler as an assembly, a court, a throne attendance or an allotment. The scene_type column says which; the deliberation column says whether the passage itself shows the gathered beings deliberating.

scene_types.assembly: Divine beings gathered to decide or be addressed on a matter
scene_types.court: Divine beings gathered to hear or judge a case, or presented before a ruler
scene_types.throne_vision: Beings attending a throne in a vision, without a stated assembly
scene_types.allotment: A distribution among divine beings stated without a narrated gathering

deliberation_states.attested: the passage shows members proposing, arguing or deciding
deliberation_states.qualified: deliberation is partial, implied or depends on restoration; see note
deliberation_states.not_stated: the passage does not show deliberation
deliberation_states.explicitly_absent: the passage denies counsel; locator required
deliberation_states.not_checked: the deliberative passage was not inspected

withdrawn.reason: The inspected edition (Rieken et al., Hethitologie Portal Mainz, CTH 344) shows a proem addressing the primeval gods and kingship passing by combat; there is no assembly, court, throne attendance or allotment. The row is withdrawn from this index; it belongs with succession myths (see the theomachy cross-references dataset).
